title: VPC & On-Prem: Kernel + Network SLEUTH Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook to triage and remediate a narrow but recurring class of failures we see in VPC and on-prem private deployments after installs and upgrades. Focus is on kernel/driver compatibility, network edge rules, and Terraform drift that cause subtle runtime failures (node not ready, GPUs invisible, slow packet drops, KV cache priming failures).

Scope and audience:
- For first/second responders on private-deploy incidents (SREs, infra eng, on-call solutions engineers).
- Not a full runbook for customer migrations; meant to complement existing smoke checklists with deeper sleuthing steps and quick scripts.

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm symptoms: exact error lines, pod/node state, and whether only model-serving pods are impacted (e.g., /infer container) or whole node. Collect logs: systemd, kubelet, containerd/docker, and the runtime logs (/var/log/redwood/*).
2) Check k8s node status: kubectl get nodes -o wide; kubectl describe node <node>. Note kernel version, taints, and Kubelet version.
3) Check GPU visibility: nvidia-smi (or rocm-smi) on host; ls -l /dev/nvidia*; kubectl logs on gpu-allocator pod.
4) Validate network reachability: curl to control-plane endpoints, DNS (nslookup), and test MTU path (ping -M do -s 1472 <peer>) to detect ICMP fragmentation.
5) Snapshot Terraform state: terraform show -json > /tmp/tf-state-snapshot.json (if using remote state, fetch with proper creds).

Common failure fingerprints and quick hypotheses:
- Node Ready flapping + kubelet OOMs: kernel memory leak or kubelet + cgroup config mismatch. Hypothesis: kernel memory cap too low after upgrade.
- GPUs not visible but driver install succeeded: kernel-driver-version mismatch or dkms module not built for current kernel.
- Sporadic RPC timeouts to control plane: MTU mismatch or iptables conntrack exhaustion.
- Post-upgrade image pullbacks and init containers stuck: container runtime overlayfs/kernel incompatibility.

Deep triage flow (ordered):
A) Kernel / driver checks
- On host: uname -a; rpm -q kernel || dpkg -l | grep linux-image; check /var/log/messages or journalctl -k -n 200.
- Confirm module for GPU: lsmod | grep nvidia; modinfo nvidia | head -n 20. If modinfo returns different version than driver package, suspect dkms failure.
- Check for hang signatures: dmesg | egrep -i "oom|hung_task|kernel panic|nv|nvidia|gpu" -n 200.
- If kernel was recently upgraded, check /boot for multiple images and the active grub entry. Some installs leave the machine on old kernel while DKMS built modules only for new kernel.

Quick remedy for dkms mismatch:
- Rebuild driver module: sudo dkms autoinstall; sudo depmod -a; sudo modprobe nvidia || sudo modprobe amdgpu. Reboot if needed.
- If air-gapped, check driver package digest on host and verify the installer used the expected package.

B) Network path and MTU
- Run: sudo ip link show; ip route show; ethtool -k <iface> to see offloads.
- Check path MTU: ping -c 3 -s 1472 -M do <control-plane-ip>. If fails, reduce packet size or patch tunnel MTU (e.g., VXLAN/Calico).
- Look for flaky TCP resets in kernel: sudo journalctl -u systemd-networkd -n 200 or sudo journalctl -k | grep RST.
- conntrack saturation: sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count and compare to nf_conntrack_max. If >80% of max, increase nf_conntrack_max temporarily and inspect NAT churn.

C) Container runtime & overlayfs
- Check containerd/docker versions and kernel compatibility table. Some overlay changes cause slow container start or stuck mounts.
- Look for mount errors: journalctl -u containerd -n 200 | egrep -i "overlay|mount|permission|no space".
- Quick workaround: restart container runtime on a drained node; if multiple nodes show the issue, investigate kernel patches affecting overlayfs.

D) Terraform drift and resource identity checks
- Terraform drift leads to mismatched security groups, route tables, or node metadata. Take tfstate snapshot and run terraform plan to detect differences (run in a scratch workspace).
- Common TF quirks: provider upgrade changed default lifecycle rule; null_resource triggers redeploy. Check module versions: cat modules/*/versions.tf and search for v0.12->v0.13 style mismatches.
- If bootstrap failed mid-upgrade, some nodes may have leftover taints/labels preventing scheduler from placing workloads. kubectl get nodes --show-labels | egrep "redwood|private-deploy" to find unexpected labels.

Hands-on quick scripts (drop-in)
- GPU verify one-liner:
  ssh root@<host> 'uname -r && nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version --format=csv' || echo "driver check failed"

- MTU path probe (host):
  python - <<'PY'
import subprocess,sys
ip='CONTROL_PLANE_IP'
for s in range(1472,1200,-28):
  r=subprocess.run(['ping','-c','1','-M','do','-s',str(s),ip],stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
  print(s, r.returncode)
PY

- TF state quick compare (local):
  terraform init -backend-config="bucket=redwood-private-tf"
  terraform workspace select prod || terraform workspace new prod
  terraform plan -out=/tmp/plan.out && terraform show -json /tmp/plan.out > /tmp/plan.json

Post-install smoke tests (explicit checks):
- Node readiness: kubectl get nodes (all Ready)
- Minimal inference flow: curl -sS -X POST http://<node-ip>:8080/v1/completions -d '{"model":"tiny-test","input":"hello"}' - should return 200 within 200ms on dedicated/private tier baseline.
- KV cache priming: run 100 short requests; monitor cache-hit metric (redwood.cache.hits) via Prometheus query. Expect >40% hit within 60s on warm nodes.
- End-to-end latency SLO: p95 < 600ms for short sequences (5-20 tokens).
- Telemetry sanity: no 5xx spikes in last 10m, token counters increment normally.

Upgrade plan (concise, safe steps):
1) Canary a single node in isolated AZ: cordon+drain, run install/upgrade, run smoke-tests above.
2) If GPU drivers/kernels changed, reboot canary node and validate nvidia modules; run 3 inference workers concurrently to stress pipeline.
3) If canary passes 30m stability window, schedule batch upgrade with rolling window and throttling (max 20% nodes at once).
4) Maintain automated rollback: retain previous AMI/image and TF workspace snapshot. If >5% error rate or any GPU driver mismatch, trigger rollback to previous image and tag the terraform workspace with failure metadata.

Rollback quick checklist:
- Revert TF change: terraform apply -refresh=false -auto-approve with previous workspace snapshot.
- Re-image affected nodes from previous image; ensure kubelet re-registers with expected labels.
- Clear pod-level caches if KV cache corrupted: restart redwood-cache sidecars in sequence.

Observability and signals to watch (where to look):
- Prometheus metrics: redwood.requests.errors, redwood.cache.hit_ratio, node_cpu_seconds, node_memory_MiB_used, node_gpu_utilization.
- Logs: kubelet (journalctl -u kubelet), container runtime, dmesg for kernel oops, /var/log/redwood/runtime.log for per-request failures.
- Network traces: tcpdump -i <iface> port 443 -w /tmp/trace.pcap for control-plane handshake issues.

Escalation template (Slack/Jira stub):
- Title: [URGENT] Private-deploy Canary Failure - <cluster> - <short symptom>
- Attached: tfstate snapshot, node uname/dmesg, nvidia-smi, kubectl get pods -A, prometheus p95/p50 for last 15m.
- Ask: Request on-call kernel/GPU ops and TF module owner.

Notes and TODOs (actionable):
- TODO: add automated dkms-verification step to post-upgrade pipeline (script + alert if mismatch).
- TODO: add path MTU test to smoke suite; include VXLAN and Calico-specific packet sizes.
- Investigate: overlayfs regressions reported in upstream kernel 6.4.x affecting containerd 1.6.x mounts.
- Draft ticket: consolidate TF provider versions across modules to prevent plan drift (target: provider v4.x).

Appendix: quick fingerprints map (short)
- "GPU invisible" -> dmesg shows 'nvidia: Unknown symbol' or lsmod missing -> likely dkms/kernel mismatch.
- "High tail latency after upgrade" -> TCP retransmits/MTU -> check MTU on tunnel interfaces.
- "Pods stuck init" -> overlay mount errors or overlayfs permission errors -> check kernel and container runtime versions.

If you use this doc, please paste failures and any local fixes in the ticket referenced above (JIRA-OPS-5678). This is a living draft; contributors welcome.
